DiamondSim

DiamondSim assigns every team a live Elo rating, simulates the rest of the season tens of thousands of times, and reports each team's odds of making — and winning — the playoffs.

  • Python
  • CustomTkinter
  • Monte Carlo
  • MLB Stats API
View source on GitHub

Gallery

What It Does

DiamondSim assigns every team a power rating using an Elo system trained on historical results, then simulates the remainder of the season tens of thousands of times to produce playoff odds, World Series odds, and a projected postseason bracket for all 30 teams.

Real MLB roster and stat data feeds player-level detail into the postseason — starting pitcher matchups, bullpen fatigue, and lineup construction — on top of the team-level Elo math. No API key or account is needed; DiamondSim pulls live schedule and score data from the public MLB Stats API.

Key Features

  • Simulate. Project the current season forward from today's live standings.
  • Backtest. Run the sim at any past date and compare predictions against the actual postseason field.
  • Dashboard. The first screen after a run: World Series favorites ranked by championship odds, plus a run summary.
  • World Series odds. Each Monte Carlo iteration plays out the full postseason bracket — Wild Card, Division Series, LCS, World Series — giving a championship probability for all 30 teams.
  • Graphs. Sortable bar charts of playoff odds, overall and by division.
  • Teams. Click any team to see its full game log, Elo history, and upcoming schedule.
  • Standings. Division tables with GB, Last 10, streak, and playoff odds; a Wild Card race with a cut-line; plus a sortable, searchable table view.
  • Statistics. Four sortable tables — Power Rankings, Run Differential, Splits, Momentum — with live search and league filtering.
  • Players. Sortable pitcher and hitter leaderboards using real MLB stats, restricted to qualified players only (MLB's own 1.0 IP / 3.1 PA per team game standard) so the list isn't dominated by two-batter call-ups.
  • Team logos. Shown throughout — the playoff bracket, Standings, the Teams tab, and the Dashboard's Favorites panel.
  • Save / Load. Save any completed run to disk and reopen it later without re-fetching or re-simulating.
  • Live progress. A progress bar tracks fetch, Elo calculation, and the Monte Carlo run; the UI stays responsive because the simulation runs on a background thread.
  • Multi-core simulation. Runs of 200+ simulations are split across every available CPU core instead of running one simulated season at a time.

How It Works

Ratings and player detail

Every team carries an Elo rating trained on historical results. On top of that team-level number, live roster and stat data adds player-level detail to the postseason simulation — starting pitcher matchups, bullpen fatigue, and lineup construction all factor into who wins a given series, not just which team is better on paper.

Monte Carlo, in parallel

Each simulated season plays out the schedule from today's actual standings — or, in Backtest mode, from any past date — all the way through a full postseason bracket, repeated tens of thousands of times. Runs of 200 or more simulations are split across every available CPU core rather than run one at a time, and the whole thing executes on a background thread so the progress bar and the rest of the interface stay responsive while it works.

No API key required

Schedule, score, roster and stat data all come from the public MLB Stats API — no account or key needed. DiamondSim is an independent project and isn't affiliated with or endorsed by MLB.

Save, load, and pick up later

A completed run can be saved to disk and reopened later without re-fetching data or re-running the simulation, so revisiting last week's projections doesn't mean waiting on tens of thousands of simulated seasons again.

For the full mechanics — the Elo formula, how player ratings blend into team strength, and the model's assumptions and limitations — see SIMULATION.md in the repository.
